HIGHLIGHTS More than three years into the crisis in Gaza, and one year into the ceasefire, displaced families are facing a fourth winter in tents. Although humanitarian assistance and commercial supplies increased following the October 2025 ceasefire, they remain insufficient against the scale of needs, and the crisis is far from over. Some 1.4 million people, or two-thirds of the population, are acutely food insecure, with deteriorating weather conditions expected to further deplete their already limited capacity to safely store food and access cooking fuel. Funding shortfalls have already forced WFP to cut monthly food assistance by one-third in Gaza and by half in the West Bank, heightening the risk of further deterioration in food security as winter compounds existing vulnerabilities.

Redevabilité : 299 plaintes et retours reçus en octobre (4 327 depuis janvier) et 1 039 visites dans les centres de ressources communautaires. Lacunes : aucune activité Abris/BNA rapportée en 2026 dans les Nippes, le Nord et le Nord-Est. L'insécurité limite l'accès à Petite-Rivière de l'Artibonite, Verrettes et Arcahaie. Synopsis (short abstract) The triannual Crop Prospects and Food Situation report provides a forward-looking global analysis of cereal production, market trends and acute food security conditions, with a particular attention on low-income food-deficit countries. FAO estimates that 41 countries/territories require external assistance for food: 31 in Africa, eight in Asia, one in Latin America and the Caribbean, and one in Europe. Persisting conflicts and insecurity remain the primary drivers of the most severe levels of acute food insecurity, while weather shocks associated with the strong El Niño event are worsening conditions in several subregions. Looking ahead, El Niño-related impacts on production are expected to remain severe into 2027 in several subregions, likely aggravating acute food insecurity further. The report also includes FAO's latest forecast for 2026 cereal production among the Low-Income Food-Deficit Countries (LIFDCs), pegged at 126.5 million tonnes, about 2 percent above both the 2025 level and the five-year average. The increase largely reflects a strong production recovery in Asia, particularly in Near East Asia, while production among African LIFDCs is expected to remain near-average.

Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. They continue to kill and maim thousands of civilians every year despite active hostilities having ended long ago. They block transport and escape routes, hinder the delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance and hamper agriculture and trade. A secret, closed-door election: Unlike the public speaker of the House vote, where lawmakers cast ballots on the chamber floor, the Senate leadership contest takes place behind closed doors. Senators vote by secret ballot, and individual votes are not disclosed. The winner only needs a caucus majority: The Democratic leadership race is decided solely by members of the party’s Senate caucus. Now that Democrats are set to have 56 seats in the new year, the winner will need secure 29 votes for the top role. Republicans choose their leaders separately: Republicans hold their own closed-door leadership elections in both chambers. events.title: UNICEF Zambia Humanitarian Flash Update No.1 (Cholera Outbreak), 16 November 2026
events.summary: Country: Zambia Source: UN Children's Fund Please refer to the attached file. Highlights Outbreak Overview : As of 16 November 2026, ZNPHI reported 3,099 cases and 68 deaths (CFR 2.2%) across 27 districts in seven provinces since 28 July. Children under 15 make up 24.9% of cases with age data (available for ~78.5% of cases). Lusaka and Chibombo are the current hotspots accounting for 75.2% of cases (1,959 and 371 respectively). Community engagement and communication : UNICEF-supported household visits reached over 1.2 million people, while dialogues engaged a further 30,000 people and 1,390 gatekeepers and influencers. This was reinforced by 31,600 communication materials (distribution underway) and a media campaign with an estimated potential audience of 7.8 million. OCV : 701,354 vaccinations supported in Lusaka, Chibombo and Chongwe (23–26 October 2026). WASH : UNICEF delivered 20 AWD kits to five districts and two tents to Chibombo for cholera treatment centres. It supported three inline chlorinators in Chibombo and WASH/IPC supplies to 20 health facilities in Chibombo and to treatment facilities in four Luapula districts. Funding : UNICEF’s cholera response 2026/27 is only 9% funded, with a US$2.95 million gap (91%); Health has the largest gap (US$1.64 million). Urgent funding is needed to replenish WASH supplies and scale up treatment and community case finding before the rainy season.
